conventions.convention: All initial states, tree topology, non-oracle operations, output wires and accepting subsets are independent of the hidden Boolean input. Input dependence enters only through XOR queries.
The address register has N bits: g_x(e_i)=x_i at one-hot addresses and g_x(a)=0 elsewhere. For N=0 the sole address is the empty word and the oracle is the identity.
An acceptance polynomial agrees with the acceptance probability on the entire Boolean cube; approximation to a promise function is required only on its promise domain.

Degree at most d means no supported monomial has degree greater than d; this includes the zero polynomial, whose formal degree is undefined. Approximate degree is minimized over all real polynomials, without a separate probability-range constraint.

Local query complexity is defined for 0 ≤ ε < 1/2 and minimizes the maximum query count over all root-to-terminal paths. Non-oracle costs and uniformity are excluded; an empty promise has complexity zero.
Branch operators are unnormalized: σ_h=w_hρ_h when the branch weight is positive, and σ_h=0 when it is zero. No conditional state is assigned to a zero-probability branch.
Symmetrization requires both a permutation-invariant promise domain and a permutation-invariant function, and uses Hamming weight |x|=Σ_i x_i.
Range height and derivative maximum are taken over the continuous interval [0,N]; probability-range bounds are assumed only at integer grid points.

load_bearing.statement: If a local bit-query algorithm makes at most T queries on every branch, then its full-cube acceptance probability is represented by a real multilinear polynomial of total degree at most 2T. Consequently, computation of f on D within error ε gives approximate degree at most 2T and query complexity at least the ceiling of half the approximate degree.

A local bit-query algorithm is a finite rooted execution tree starting in the all-zero state, with input-independent topology, non-oracle unitaries and instruments, and terminal output rules. Queries are the specified one-hot-address XOR oracle, and every path has at most T query nodes for a T-query algorithm.

For any execution history h containing t(h) oracle calls, every matrix entry of its unnormalized branch operator on the Boolean cube is represented by a complex polynomial with no supported monomial of total degree greater than 2t(h). Finite input-independent instrument branches are allowed.

For a permutation-invariant Boolean domain D and permutation-invariant function f, an ε-approximating real polynomial of total degree at most d yields a univariate real polynomial q of degree at most d such that q(|x|) also ε-approximates f on D.
If p is a real polynomial with no supported monomial of degree greater than d ∈ N₀ and h=max p−min p on [−1,1], then max |p′| ≤ d²h/2. The zero polynomial is allowed.
For an integer N≥1 and a real polynomial q with 0≤q(k)≤1 at integers k=0,…,N, let h=max q−min q and D=max |q′| on [0,N]. Then D≥max{0,h−1}.
For N≥1 and a real polynomial q supported in degrees at most d ∈ N₀, with 0≤q(k)≤1 at integers k=0,…,N, its continuous range height h and derivative maximum D on [0,N] satisfy D≤d²h/N.

concerns.concern: The Statement's consequence says 'if it computes f:D→{0,1} with error at most ε' and then displays Q^bit_ε, without specifying 0≤ε<1/2. The cited def-qa-15-bit-oracle-query-complexity defines that quantity only for this range, whereas approximate degree is defined for every ε≥0. Explicitly qualify the query-complexity consequence by its defined error range; the acceptance-polynomial and approximate-degree conclusions do not need the upper restriction.

seams_checked.note: The supplier's standard query is a total-address XOR unitary. The local model instantiates it with the explicitly total one-hot address function, and the amplitude, density and example calculations use exactly this action. No controlled-access capability or gate-cost bound is inferred.

Checked the task/promise, finite branch law, quantum-query algorithm and query-cost definitions against their uses. The local model specializes to all-zero initialization and hidden-input-independent operations and predicates; the page correctly distinguishes a specified algorithm's cost from minimization over algorithms. Off-promise approximation and finite instrument branches retain the supplier conventions.

The supplier's base computation model allows encoded classical inputs and a total input-dependent predicate, with full-list uniformity imposed separately. Through the query-model specialization, this page explicitly excludes access to the hidden encoding and fixes its predicate independently of that encoding. It imports terminal marginalization and zero-work-register conventions without claiming uniformity or transferring circuit-time bounds.
